Shafiq Ahmed with S. A. Rahim ----- For the Petitioner.

Chandpur Tea Company Ltd. ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Joint Secretary & ors. ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
SM Hussain J: Chandpur Tea Company Ltd. being the petitioner in Writ petition No. 427 of 1977 has challenged the legality of certain Certificate cases allegedly on the ground that in view of the provisions of section 142 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the recovery of arrear rents dues therein was barred by limitation. The Certificate cases arose out of non-payment of the balance dues of rent after the final publication of the records of right. The petitioner was assessed provisionally under sub-section (1) of section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The petitioner bad was paying such provisional rent till such time when such rent was finally determined under sub-section (3) of section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. After adjustment of rent with the previous years the petitioner was served with a demand notice to pay the balance dues being the determining enhanced rent. The petitioner having failed to pay the balance dues of rent the impugned certificate cases were instituted by the Revenue Authority against which the petitioner moved this Court and obtained this Rule under disposal. 

 2. So far as the impugned certificate cases are concerned they relate to certain Tea gar-dens situated in the district of Sylhet. In such circumstances, the limitation for the recovery of arrear rent dues is governed by the provisions of section 142 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with sub-section (4a) of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Section 142 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides that the period of limitation for the recovery of arrear rent shall be three years running from last day of the year in which the arrear fell due. Sub-section (4a) of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act further provides that in computing the period of limitation for the recovery of any arrear of rent in the district of Sylhet, a period of twenty-four months that is two years shall be excluded on and from the date of acquisition of the rent receiving interest to which such arrear relate. Reading the aforesaid provisions of section 142 and sub-section (4a) of section 3 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act together it clearly appears that the period of limitation for the purpose of recovery of arrear rent with regard to any land in the district of Sylhet extended up to a period of five years from the last day of the year in which such arrear fell due. 

 3. In this connection reference may be made to the provisions of clause (ff) of subsection (4) of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which provides for the obligation of every owner of any land to pay rent to the Government at the enhanced rate, if any, after the final determination of the rent under sub-section (3) of section 19 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act and in such case the tenant in question shall be liable to pay the balance with retrospective effect from the notified date that is the date of final publication of the records of right under sub-section (3) of section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Thus it will appear that once the rate of rent is finally determined and published in the final records of right under sub-section (3) of section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, any balance dues there under can be recoverable with retrospective effect from the date of such final publication of the records of right under sub-section (3) of section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So for the purpose of prospective realisation of rent at the final rate the time for limitation shall run from notified date that is, the date of final publication of the records of right under sub-section (3) of section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. That being so inevitably the aforesaid period of limitation as provided under section 142 read with sub-section (4a) of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act shall normally be a period of five years with regard to any land situated in the district of Sylhet from the date of the final publication of the records of right of that area under sub-section (3) of section 19 of the State Acquisition. and Tenancy Act. 

 4. The only question now remaining for consideration is whether such period of limitation of five years as aforesaid from the date of the final publication of the records of right is an absolute period or is subject to any extension under section 19 of the Limitation Act. In this connection reference may be made to the provision of section 151(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act wherein it has been provided that apart from sections 6, 7, 8 and 9 and sub-section (2) of section 19 of the Limitation Act all the remaining provisions of the Limitation Act shall apply as far as possible to all suits, appeals and applications arising under Part V of the said State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, but subject to the provisions of the said Part V of the said State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. From the aforesaid provisions of section 151(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it clearly appears that the provisions of section 19 will be applicable in any application arising under Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Therefore, unless it is found that the provisions of section 19 of the Limitation Act is repugnant to any of the provisions of Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the said provisions of section 19 of the Limitation Act shall be applicable in any application arising under Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The present proceeding admittedly having taken place under Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, section 19 of the Limitation Act applied in the present case in full force. 

 5. Section 19(1) of Limitation Act provides that where before the expiration of the period prescribed for an application in respect of any right, an acknowledgement of liability in respect of such right has been made in writing by the parties against whom such right is claimed, a fresh period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the acknowledgement was so made. In the present case since the draft publication of the records of right and the provisional determination of the fate of rent, the petitioner had all along paid the provisional rent to the Revenue Authority of the Government periodical and successively every year and such payment of provisional rent continued even after the publication of the records of right and final determination of the rate of rent. Such payment of provisional rent every year by way of a "treasury chalan" signed by the petitioner in favour of the Government bore an acknowledgement on the part of the petitioner its liability to pay the enhanced rate finally from time to time. This has created a legal obligation on the petitioner to pay the enhanced rate of part of the rent as finally determined and published in the record of right under sub-section (3) of Section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. This payment from year to year is a clear acknowledgement on the part of the petitioner about its liability to pay the enhanced rate of rent when so finally determined and by making such payment every year the period of limitation was extended from year to year by way of an acknowledgement as contemplated under section 19 of the Limitation Act. That being so for the purpose of computing the period of limitation in the present case, it shall run from the date of the last payment of provisional dues, by the petitioner in favour of the Government by way of "treasury chalan" and shall continue till the completion of five years from such date where after any recovery of arrear rent shall be barred."
